proposal.title: Define Logix digital video standard with chronological profiles
proposal.reason: Revise the existing kind proposal to distinguish the core contract, optional profiles and implementation qualification. Preserve all existing specification chapters and values; add an explicit scope statement without inventing protocol versions or completed qualification.

specification.description:
The host negotiates a raster the monitor can actually display before enabling the picture. Capability failures require an explicit safe profile; connection alone does not establish a supported resolution.

Baseline monitors accept vertical-retrace palette commands. From NCC June 1982, explicitly capable Color Pro monitors also accept bounded horizontal-retrace commands under technology.scanline_palette_list; do not send these to legacy monitors.

Host firmware performs selection using controller control-channel registers; monitor fixed capability ROM/straps and serializer.

Use an explicitly configured profile or documented common safe raster; otherwise remain blank. Never infer 640-pixel support from connection alone.

The Control pair is half-duplex and bidirectional.

Startup proceeds in this order: blank the picture; read the versioned capability record with an integrity check and timeout; intersect host and monitor raster support; select the raster and initialise the palette; then enable the picture.

The capability record contains {Control channel capability fields}. The horizontal-retrace extension is defined by {Horizontal palette extension reference}.

specification.description:
Raster {ID} displays {Active width} by {Active height} active pixels at {Pixel clock MHz} MHz. The total pixel and line counts below include blanking.

Including blanking, each line contains {Horizontal total pixels} pixels and each frame contains {Vertical total lines} lines.

Raster {ID} displays {Active width} by {Active height} active pixels at {Pixel clock MHz} MHz. The total pixel and line counts below include blanking.

Including blanking, each line contains {Horizontal total pixels} pixels and each frame contains {Vertical total lines} lines.

Raster {ID} displays {Active width} by {Active height} active pixels at {Pixel clock MHz} MHz. Its frame rate is {Frame rate Hz} Hz. The raster is progressive.

Including blanking, each line contains {Horizontal total pixels} pixels and each frame contains {Vertical total lines} lines. The horizontal frequency is {Horizontal frequency kHz} kHz.

Logical image sizes and palette indices must be mapped explicitly to the selected output. A wider logical mode cannot be forced onto a monitor that lacks the required raster.

Integer horizontal/vertical pixel repetition, including sprites. 160/320-wide logical modes can repeat to 320/640; 100 lines repeat to 200. Reject 640-wide graphics or 80-column text on a 320-only monitor; software viewport is a separately reported service. Artemis card repeats legacy pixels/lines to {Professional output raster} for Mono Pro; never downscales 400 lines to an old monitor.

Explicit 1-bit and 2-bit pixel-to-output-index maps. Color indices are not brightness values. On grayscale displays map RGB palette entries to luminance; Mono I direct DAC requires host index mapping.

The Aurelia June 1978 baseline, later Artemis raster profiles and June 1982 horizontal-retrace palette extension are distinct scopes. Raster sizes are capability profiles, not protocol version numbers. Monitor/controller support must be intersected; a new resolution or palette feature is not automatically present on old monitors. Hardware-specific scaling examples remain explanatory, not universal requirements. The professional 800×600 integration recorded in June 1982 is not silently added to this record’s currently specified raster tables; its exact link/timing contract requires separate review.
